lessons: Inventory scarcity (count water, count biscuit) is its own scene.
Starvation degrades cognition before killing body.
Cannibalism arises only after days of nothing; has moral cost.
food_and_water.use_in_our_film: Show protagonist counting and rationing at least once.

lessons: Sealed holds and huts are cinematic and cheap to render.
Climate can be ally (mild California removes winter as threat).
shelter_and_weather.use_in_our_film: Pick climate that lets us focus on social rather than weather threats.

lessons: Surgical scars and bandages make visual continuity ledger (Moreau).
injuries_illness_exhaustion.use_in_our_film: Use one specific injury (lacerated foot, twisted ankle) and track healing across scenes.

lessons: Islands with one boat concentrate dramatic stakes.
Single exit makes escape choices consequential.
navigation_and_escape.use_in_our_film: Single exit (one boat, one trail, one road).

lessons: Biggest scarcity can be knowledge (Scarlet Plague) or information (Moreau), not food.
resource_scarcity.use_in_our_film: Make knowledge/information the deepest scarcity under surface scarcity.

lessons: Protagonist should misread threat at least twice before understanding.
Most dangerous threat is one dressed in friendship.
Small kindness can be deadly error (keeping contagious corpse for night).
